comment: Closed registry of stable SKG parse-error codes. Conformance fixtures assert these instead of message substrings, because implementations word the same failure differently. Adding a code here is the only way to make it usable in a fixture; every implementation checks its own code set against this file. See docs/conformance.md.

codes.summary: A byte appeared where no token can start.
A string literal reached a raw newline or end of input before its closing quote.
A backslash escape other than \" \\ \n \t appeared inside a quoted string.
A ':' was required and something else was found.
A '}' was required and something else was found.
A ']' was required and something else was found.
A quoted string was required (skg_version, schema_version, import path) and something else was found.
An identifier was required and something else was found.
A field value was required and the token could not start one.
An identifier was not followed by ':', '{' or '['.
A token was required whose kind has no more specific code.
A '{' block reached end of input before its '}'. Also used for an unterminated block inside a block array.
A block array reached end of input before its ']'.
A scalar array reached end of input before its ']'.
Array elements did not all share one type tag.
An integer literal did not fit a signed 64-bit integer.
A float literal could not be converted to a 64-bit float.
skg_version was declared more than once.
schema_version was declared more than once.
skg_version was not a MAJOR.MINOR pair of decimal numbers.
skg_version was well formed but newer than the parser implements.
A bracketed import list reached end of input before its ']'.
The 'import' keyword was not followed by a string or '['.
Blocks, block arrays and arrays nested deeper than 128 levels.
The input exceeded the 10 MiB per-file cap.
An import cycle was reached. Only a parser with the 'imports' capability can produce this.
An imported file could not be opened. Only a parser with the 'imports' capability can produce this.
Imports nested deeper than the implementation's import-chain cap. Reserved: no implementation enforces a chain cap yet, so no fixture asserts it. See docs/conformance.md 'Known gaps'.
Fallback for a diagnostic that reached the caller without a code. Never valid in a fixture - its appearance is a parser bug.
